::::

I design, build, and ship **production LLM systems** end to end — from shaping the solution with clients in pre-sales through architecture, implementation, cloud deployment, and knowledge transfer. My focus is the layers that decide whether an LLM system works in production: **evaluation, retrieval and data design, and compliance**. I build evaluation harnesses that show where accuracy is lost, use them to drive architecture and roadmap decisions, and benchmark model, cost, and latency trade-offs up front.

I have worked remotely with US companies delivering agentic AI to clients in healthcare, travel, media, and real estate: HIPAA-compliant document pipelines, multimodal document automation integrated with ERPs, NL2SQL and RAG assistants, and real-time voice agents that handle calls and operate web applications. Before that, I spent years in industrial AI in Brazil taking ML from prototype to production — predictive maintenance and MLOps on AWS for wind turbines, and edge ML, computer vision, and IoT products. Earlier still, I did academic research on **Bayesian optimization, Monte Carlo Tree Search, and multi-objective evolutionary algorithms** (Best Student Paper Award, EMO 2019), and hold a Master's in Engineering from Shinshu University as a MEXT Government Scholar.

I am looking to lead AI engineering and system architecture: setting technical direction, making trade-offs explicit, working closely with clients and stakeholders, and raising the engineering bar of the teams I work with.

## Research {#research}

::: {.role}
### University of Warwick, Warwick Business School {.role-title}
[Doctoral Research]{.role-sub} [Coventry, United Kingdom · Oct 2019 – Apr 2022]{.role-meta}

Ranking & selection, Bayesian optimization, and reinforcement learning. Investigated sample-efficient policy learning for constrained supply chain scheduling of biopharmaceutical products, developing Multi-Objective MCTS using marginal hypervolume as the selection criterion. Under Prof. Juergen Branke, collaborated with Prof. Chun-Hung Chen on two-stage ranking-and-selection, extending OCBA and Expected Value of Information algorithms.
:::

::: {.role}
### Shinshu University {.role-title}
[MSc Research]{.role-sub} [Nagano, Japan · Apr 2017 – Mar 2019]{.role-meta}

Developed a predictive model approximating complex decision space geometries caused by difficult Pareto set topologies, significantly improving MOEA solution distribution and convergence. Collaborated across the International Associated Laboratory LIA-MODO (Shinshu, Inria France, UAM Mexico), culminating in multiple publications and the Best Student Paper Award at EMO 2019.
:::
